verdict.rationale: vLLM documents its own mechanisms for serving concurrent requests efficiently: continuous batching of incoming requests, advanced scheduling for peak GPU utilization, and PagedAttention KV-cache memory management. A community user confirms they build on its KV cache and continuous batching. However, nothing in the evidence shows the runtime reserving dedicated capacity per agent or session, or guaranteeing steady throughput under contention. Missing for 10: documented capacity reservation or isolation per session/agent, QoS or fairness guarantees under concurrent load, and independent evidence of stable throughput across multiple concurrent clients.

support.subject: As a power-user, I know the runtime reserves dedicated capacity so throughput holds steady when multiple agents or sessions issue requests concurrently
